svg.title: Choosing a Power BI Semantic Model Storage Mode
svg.desc: A decision tree diagram for selecting between Import, DirectQuery, and Direct Lake storage modes per table, detailing the Direct Lake flavor choice and the silent SQL view fallback trap.
svg.text: Choosing a Power BI Semantic Model Storage Mode
Per-Table Selection Framework · Import vs DirectQuery vs Direct Lake · OneLake vs SQL Flavor · Fallback Traps

g.title: What does this table need? — Root question: pick a storage mode per table from freshness need and data location.
g.text: Root Decision: What Does Each Table in the Model Require?
Evaluate by freshness requirements, data residency (OneLake Delta vs external), volume, and DAX calculation complexity:
A. Periodic snapshot acceptable, needs fast DAX ➔ Import
B. Source must stay live / strict data compliance ➔ DirectQuery
C. Data lives in OneLake Delta, zero refresh wanted ➔ Direct Lake

g.title: Import — Data copied into an in-memory VertiPaq model; needs a refresh schedule to stay current.
g.text: 1. IMPORT (MANAGED VERTIPAQ COPY)
In-Memory Columnar VertiPaq
• Highest query throughput & sub-second visual rendering
• 100% full DAX, time intelligence, and M expression support
Operational Profile & Rules:
✓ Freshness: Point-in-time snapshot refreshed on cadence
✓ Size Limits: 1 GB default (expanded via Large Format)
✓ Desktop Limit: 10 GB fixed PBIX upload ceiling
✓ XMLA write tooling supported under Large Format
Standard: Best for complex dimensions & small-to-mid facts
Watch-outs & Refresh Bottlenecks:
❌ Data duplication into VertiPaq storage
❌ Multi-hour refresh runtimes on massive transaction tables
❌ OOM risk if refresh memory approaches 50% capacity SKU
Trap: Authoring full Import models for billion-row lake facts
Use Direct Lake on OneLake to eliminate refresh entirely.
Decision Fit:
Complex dimension tables with heavy Power Query cleansing,
small-to-medium facts (<100M rows), and executive dashboards.

g.title: DirectQuery — Every query forwards to the source, so results always reflect current data — at a latency cost.
g.text: 2. DIRECTQUERY (LIVE SOURCE PUSHDOWN)
Zero Model Data Cache
• Translates DAX into SQL on every visual interaction
• Always 100% current source of truth with zero delay
Operational Profile & Rules:
✓ Freshness: Real-time (sub-second source updates reflect live)
✓ Security: Inherits source RLS and database permissions
✓ Gateway: Heavy gateway utilization for on-prem DBs
✓ Zero scheduled refresh operations to monitor
Standard: Best for high-frequency operational telemetry
Watch-outs & Performance Penalties:
❌ Visual load times limited by source database responsiveness
❌ Complex DAX formulas fail to fold into single SQL queries
❌ Concurrent report users generate heavy load on source DB
Trap: Underestimating Gateway capacity on busy dashboards
Configure aggregation tables to buffer high-frequency scans.
Decision Fit:
Live transactional feeds requiring sub-minute freshness,
strict data residency mandates, or systems with source RLS.

g.title: Direct Lake — Reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, on demand, with no import copy and no refresh schedule.
g.text: 3. DIRECT LAKE (ONELAKE ZERO-COPY)
Direct Delta Lake Parquet Reads
• Queries Delta tables in OneLake directly with 0 data copy
• Lazy on-demand column loading on first query touch
Operational Profile & Rules:
✓ Freshness: Current as of framing (metadata rebind in seconds)
✓ Throughput: VertiPaq-like speed once columns reside in RAM
✓ Composite Support: Mixes Direct Lake facts with Import dims
✓ Zero data duplication or import refresh runtime overhead
Standard: Default mode for all Microsoft Fabric Lakehouses
Flavor Sub-Decision Required:
• Direct Lake forks into TWO distinct runtime flavors:
1. Direct Lake on OneLake (ADLS native connector, 0 fallback)
2. Direct Lake on SQL (SQL Analytics Endpoint mediated)
Trap: Direct Lake on SQL can silently fall back to DirectQuery!
See Flavor Resolution below before publishing model.
Decision Fit:
Multi-million and billion-row Lakehouse / Warehouse Gold
Delta tables requiring high-speed enterprise analytical BI.

g.title: Which Direct Lake flavor? — Sub-decision: Direct Lake on OneLake (default) vs Direct Lake on SQL (security/fallback needs).
g.text: Direct Lake Flavor Resolution: OneLake vs SQL Endpoint
Choose the runtime connector based on security model & fallback requirements
Direct Lake on OneLake (Default)
• Uses ADLS storage connector
• Direct OneLake RBAC security checks
• Created by default in Desktop & Service
✓ STRUCTURALLY CANNOT FALL BACK
Fastest query path with 0 SQL check latency.
Direct Lake on SQL Endpoint
• Uses SQL Server / SqlAnalytics connector
• Evaluates SQL RLS under delegated identity
• Created from SQL Analytics Endpoint page
⚠️ SUPPORTS TRANSPARENT DQ FALLBACK
Needed for SQL RLS / delegated identity.
Selection Rule & Best Practice:
• Default to Direct Lake on OneLake for maximum query performance and zero fallback risk.
• Use Direct Lake on SQL only when T-SQL Row-Level Security (RLS) under delegated identity is mandatory.
• Verify the connector in TMDL view (`AzureStorage` vs `SqlAnalytics`) to confirm model flavor.

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL views force DirectQuery fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL views force DirectQuery fallback — A Direct Lake on SQL table built on a SQL view silently forces every query into DirectQuery fallback.
g.text: CRITICAL MODELING TRAP
SQL Views Silently Force DirectQuery Fallback
Tables built on SQL views bypass Direct Lake storage entirely
The Silent Performance Regression Mechanism:
• Direct Lake cannot transcode virtual SQL views into OneLake Parquet memory pages.
• Every report visual touching a view-based table falls back to live DirectQuery execution!
The model still reports 'Direct Lake' in the Power BI Portal UI!
Architectural Fix & Design Rule:
• Fix: Base Direct Lake model tables strictly on BASE DELTA TABLES, never SQL views.
• Push view transformation logic upstream into materialized Gold Delta tables using Spark/SQL.
Golden Standard: Direct Lake = Direct Delta Base Table Reads!
Never scale capacity SKUs to fix slowness caused by an accidental view fallback.
